newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bolsa ends almost flat in token volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bolsa ends almost flat in token volume.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed Friday almost with no change with token volume in a very subdued and cautious market, dealers said.

"There were virtually no deals today," Carlos Gil, trader for Banco Republica said. "The local bolsa was following with attention turbulences of the Mexican peso and a steady decline today of the Brazilian stock market, and is still awaiting a clearer domestic political scenario."
The Mexican peso fell about 2.5 percent this week. Brazil's Bovespa index Friday declined 1.3 percent.
Argentina's leading MerVal index slipped 0.25 percent, closing at 559.57. Volume shrank to $10.5 million from Thursday's already low level of $15.6 million.

The market has also been affected by an ongoing bickering between former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo and administration officials over his charges of corruption in the government. But Gil said that although that was a negative factor, its weight over the market was declining.
Miguel Daneri, of Boston Securities, said the market was "virtually paralized considering the domestic political front is not yet completely clear."
And traders said those factors, plus caution over the upcoming presidential elections in the United States, meant the subdued tone may remain in place at least for a few more days.
Daneri added: "Pension funds are still awaiting a clearer landscape to plunge into the market. The year is nearing to its end and they dont't want to take big risks."
